readings.title: Job's Reply: The Majesty of El
readings.subtitle: God's Power Over Creation
readings.text: [Job 26:1] And Iyoḇ answered and said: [2] “How have you helped the powerless? How have you saved the arm that has no strength? [3] “How have you counselled the unwise? And how much sound wisdom have you declared? [4] “To <dn>את</dn> whom have you uttered words? And whose spirit came from you? [5] “The dead tremble, those under the waters and those inhabiting them. [6] “Sheol is naked before <dn>Him</dn>, and Abaddon has no covering. [7] “<dn>He</dn> stretches out the north over empty space; <dn>He</dn> hangs the earth on nothing. [8] “Binding up water in <dn>His</dn> thick clouds, yet the clouds are not torn under them. [9] “Covering the face of <dn>His</dn> throne, spreading <dn>His</dn> cloud over it. [10] “<dn>He</dn> drew a limit on the surface of the waters, at the boundary of light and darkness. [11] “The columns of the heavens tremble, and are stunned at <dn>His</dn> reproof. [12] “By <dn>His</dn> power <dn>He</dn> has calmed the sea, and by <dn>His</dn> understanding <dn>He</dn> struck down Rahaḇ. [13] “By <dn>His</dn> Spirit <dn>He</dn> adorned the heavens; <dn>His</dn> hand pierced the fleeing serpent. [14] “See, these are the fringes of <dn>His</dn> ways; and how little a word we hear of <dn>Him</dn>! And who understands the thunder of <dn>His</dn> might?”

readings.title: Job Maintains His Integrity
readings.subtitle: The Portion of the Wicked Man
readings.text: [Job 27:1] And Iyoḇ continued his discourse, and said: [2] “As <dn>El</dn> lives, who has turned aside my right-ruling, and the <dn>Almighty</dn>, who has made my life bitter, [3] “As long as my breath is in me, and the spirit of <dn>Eloah</dn> is in my nostrils, [4] “My lips do not speak unrighteousness, nor my tongue mutter deceit. [5] “Far be it from me that I should declare you right; till I die I shall not turn aside my integrity from me. [6] “I have held fast to my righteousness, and I do not let it go; my heart does not reproach me as long as I live. [7] “Let my enemy be like the wrong one, and he who rises up against me like the unrighteous. [8] “For what is the expectancy of the defiled one, when <dn>He</dn> cuts off, when <dn>Eloah</dn> takes away his life? [9] “Does <dn>El</dn> hear his cry when distress comes upon him? [10] “Does he delight himself in the <dn>Almighty</dn>? Does he call on <dn>Eloah</dn> at all times? [11] “I teach <dn>את</dn> you concerning the hand of <dn>El</dn>; I do not hide what is with the <dn>Almighty</dn>. [12] “See, all of you have seen it; why then do you act so vainly? [13] “This is the portion of a wrong man with <dn>El</dn>, and the inheritance of cruel ones, which they receive from the <dn>Almighty</dn>: [14] “If his children increase, it is for the sword; and his offspring are not satisfied with bread. [15] “Those who survive him are buried in death, and their widows do not weep. [16] “Though he heaps up silver like dust, and piles up garments like clay – [17] “He piles it up, but the righteous wears it, and the innocent divides the silver. [18] “He shall build his house like a moth, like a booth which a watchman made. [19] “The rich man lies down, but not gathered; he opens his eyes, and he is no more. [20] “Terrors overtake him like a flood; a whirlwind steals him away in the night. [21] “The east wind lifts him up, and he is gone; for it whirls him out of his place. [22] “And it casts at him without sparing; he flees strictly from its hand. [23] “It claps its hands at him, and hisses him out of his place.

readings.title: The Search for Wisdom
readings.subtitle: Man Mines the Earth, But Wisdom is from God
readings.text: [Job 28:1] “For there is a mine for silver, and a place where gold is refined. [2] “Iron is taken from the earth, and copper is smelted from ore. [3] “Man puts an end to darkness, and searches every limit, stones in the gloom and death-shadow. [4] “He breaks open a shaft away from the people; the forgotten places, away from feet; they hang, they swing to and fro, far from men. [5] “Earth, out of which comes food, shall be turned up underneath as by fire. [6] “Its stones are the source of sapphires, and it has dust of gold. [7] “The path no bird of prey knows, nor has the falcon’s eye seen it. [8] “The proud lions have not trodden it, nor has the fierce lion passed over it. [9] “He has put his hand on the flint; He has overturned the mountains at the roots. [10] “He has cut out channels in the rocks, and his eye has seen every precious matter. [11] “He has dammed up the streams from trickling, and brought what is hidden to light. [12] “But wisdom, where is it found? And where is the place of understanding? [13] “Man has not known its value, nor is it found in the land of the living. [14] “The deep said, ‘It is not in me’; and the sea said, ‘It is not with me.’ [15] “Gold is not given for it, nor is silver weighed for its price. [16] “It is not valued in the gold of Ophir, in precious shoham or sapphire. [17] “Gold and crystal do not equal it, nor is it exchanged for a vessel of fine gold. [18] “Coral and crystal are not mentioned; and the acquisition of wisdom is above rubies. [19] “The topaz of Kush does not equal it, nor is it valued in pure gold. [20] “From where then does wisdom come? And where is the place of understanding? [21] “It has been hidden from the eyes of all living, and concealed from the birds of the heavens. [22] “Abaddon and Death have said, ‘We have heard a report of it with our ears.’ [23] “<dn>Elohim</dn> understands its way, and <dn>He</dn> knows its place. [24] “For <dn>He</dn> looks to the ends of the earth, sees under all the heavens, [25] “To make a weight for the wind, and <dn>He</dn> weighed the waters by measure. [26] “When <dn>He</dn> made a law for the rain, and a way for the lightning of thunder, [27] “Then <dn>He</dn> saw it and declared it; <dn>He</dn> prepared it, indeed, <dn>He</dn> searched it out. [28] “And to man <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>‘See, the fear of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, that is wisdom, and to turn from evil is understanding.’</dq> ”

readings.title: Job Recalls His Former Glory
readings.subtitle: Days of Respect and Prosperity
readings.text: [Job 29:1] And Iyoḇ continued his discourse, and said: [2] “Oh, that I were as in months past, as in the days when <dn>Eloah</dn> watched over me; [3] “When <dn>His</dn> lamp shone upon my head, and by <dn>His</dn> light I walked through darkness; [4] “As I was in the days of my autumn, when the intimacy of <dn>Eloah</dn> was over my tent; [5] “When the <dn>Almighty</dn> was yet with me, my children around me; [6] “When my steps were bathed with cream, and the rock poured out rivers of oil for me! [7] “When I went out to the gate by the city, when I took my seat in the open square, [8] “The young men saw me and hid, and the aged rose up and stood; [9] “The rulers refrained from talking, and laid their hand on their mouth; [10] “The voice of nobles was hushed, and their tongue stuck to the roof of their mouth. [11] “For the ear heard, and declared me blessed, and the eye saw, and bore witness to me; [12] “Because I delivered the poor who cried out, and the fatherless who had no helper. [13] “The blessing of a perishing man came upon me, and I caused the widow’s heart to sing for joy. [14] “I put on righteousness, and it clothed me; my right-ruling was like a robe and a turban. [15] “I was eyes to the blind, and I was feet to the lame. [16] “I was a father to the poor, and I investigated the case which I did not know. [17] “And I broke the jaws of the unrighteous, and plucked the prey from his teeth. [18] “Then I said, ‘I shall die in my nest, and multiply days as the sand. [19] ‘My root is spread out to the waters, and the dew lies all night on my branch. [20] ‘My esteem is fresh within me, and my bow is renewed in my hand.’ [21] “They listened to me and waited, and kept silent for my counsel. [22] “After my words they did not speak again, and my speech settled on them as dew. [23] “And they waited for me as for the rain, and they opened their mouth wide as for the latter rain. [24] “If I laughed at them, they did not believe it; and the light of my face they did not cast down. [25] “I chose the way for them, and sat as chief. And I dwelt as a sovereign in the army, as one who comforts mourners.
